transcript_text:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood PM), Priya Menon (DeltaForge Head of Platform), Carlos Diaz (DevOps), Liam O'Neill (Security), Zoe Park (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick technical sync to validate marketplace connector and helm packaging for DeltaForge private VPC onboarding. Main topics: helm operator compat, KMS/HSM constraints, VPC peering, firewall/NAT rules, UAT benchmark scheduling, packaging checklist for marketplace listing. Action items defined, next steps to share runbook and schedule UAT.

Topics:
- Marketplace connector packaging and helm values
- VPC peering and network egress patterns
- KMS/HSM and encryption at rest expectations
- Load/latency profile for UAT
- Rollout and failover behavior (multi-region)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, i'm maya from Redwood, i've got ethan our se and nora product on the call. how's everybody?
[00:08] Priya Menon: Hey Maya, hi team. Busy week but excited to get this across the line.
[00:12] Carlos Diaz: Morning, afternoon — depending where you are — Carlos here. we'll try to keep this focused on the helm/operator bits.
[00:18] Ethan Ruiz: Awesome. my goal today is to get a working checklist so you can install the connector in your UAT VPC with minimum friction and then run a lightweight perf pass.
[00:27] Zoe Park: we have some product folks who want to understand failover behavior if a region goes down.
[00:33] Liam O'Neill: hi, quick note from security, we have KMS requirements and audit log fields we need to see. we'll talk through that.

[00:45] Speaker 6: (inaudible) 
[00:50] Maya Chen: i'll start with a quick overview of the connector packaging approach — apologies if this is a repeat — but theres two delivery paths: 1) marketplace listing where we provide a packaged helm chart + operator and 2) direct private deployment tarball for air-gapped installs. for marketplace listings we include a values.yaml template that maps to marketplace parameters, and we also support a separate helm operator for upgrades.
[01:12] Priya Menon: Can you clarify how the values map to our internal secrets manager? we use Vault currently.
[01:18] Ethan Ruiz: yeah good question, so we have three integration patterns: KMS (cloud provider KMS), customer-managed KMS via external key encryption (we support wrapping keys), and secret injection from vault via CSI driver. the helm chart has toggles: enableKMS: true/false, useCSIForSecrets: true/false, vaultPath: <path>. there's a sample for vault token mounting in the runbook. note, the CSI flow requires the cluster to have the CSI secrets store mounted, we provide an example sidecar.
[01:44] Carlos Diaz: sidecar adds complexity, do you have minimal footprint option? We want to avoid adding more service accounts and cluster roles if possible.
[01:49] Ethan Ruiz: yes, for customers who don't want CSI we recommend pre-provisioning secrets into k8s sealedsecrets or using the KMS-based key wrapping. SealedSecrets is actually what a lot of our larger customers use. it's a one-time step during install.
[02:05] Priya Menon: What about network egress? do calls go over the internet to redwood hosted control plane or is it pure VPC?
[02:11] Maya Chen: good point. For Private deployments we can run the control plane in your VPC (private control plane), but for the marketplace connector when installed in standard mode it will reach back to Redwood endpoints over TLS. we have an option for a VPC peering arrangement and a private link type pattern. we documented that in the marketplace networking guide but we'll re-share.
[02:28] Zoe Park: is there a difference if we do the Dedicated contract vs the marketplace install? latency wise I mean.
[02:34] Ethan Ruiz: Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and lower cross-tenant risk; in terms of connector behavior the helm install is the same but the backend endpoints you point to differ. for dedicated we'll provide endpoints in the Dedicated pool and we can arrange interconnects. For marketplace installs you can choose to route through Redwoods hosted endpoints or set up private link.
[02:52] Liam O'Neill: For compliance, we need to ensure audit logs contain user id, request id, model id, and redaction markers. Is that in the telemetry?
[02:59] Nora Patel: we emit token-level and request-level traces; our audit payload includes request id and user id mapping but i want to flag that there are some flags we toggled historically that may trim prompt text for PII. we can provide schema.
[03:14] Priya Menon: okay can we get that schema and a sample log with redactions?
[03:19] Maya Chen: yes, will include in the security appendix.
[03:22] Carlos Diaz: quick question about helm version compatibility — we run 1.8 currently with a managed cluster. any known incompat?
[03:28] Ethan Ruiz: tested up to 1.9, backward to 1.7 we'll aim for 1.6+. there are CRD upgrade steps, we ship a preflight check job that runs CRD validation. i'll attach the preflight logs.
[03:40] Speaker 6: um (mumble)
[03:44] Maya Chen: moving on — UAT perf profile. what are your expected concurrency and latency SLOs?
[03:49] Priya Menon: for first pass we want to validate 100 rps with p95 < 250ms for embeddings-ish calls, and gen calls maybe 10 rps with p95 < 600ms. not absolute yet.
[03:58] Ethan Ruiz: that's reasonable for a two-node test cluster if you pick a quantized model. For unquantized base models you may see higher latency. we recommend a model variant with int8 quantization for UAT. we also will suggest batching window settings.
[04:12] Zoe Park: is there any model caching that needs to be pre-warmed? we've seen cold start issues before.
[04:17] Ethan Ruiz: yes the KV cache population matters. our installer includes a warm-up job that pre-populates the KV cache and pulls the quantized model shards into local disk cache. that job is optional but recommended before perf runs.
[04:29] Carlos Diaz: disk IO — do you require NVMe? our EBS baseline is gp3.
[04:34] Ethan Ruiz: we support gp3 but for best throughput NVMe local is preferred. our runbook notes recommended disk throughput for target rps. we'll include that table.
[04:44] Liam O'Neill: How about KMS/HSM: we need HSM-backed keys for production. do you integrate with Cloud HSM or only provider KMS?
[04:53] Maya Chen: we have integrations with AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM, and we also support bringing-your-own-HSM via PKCS#11 if you run private. there are additional steps in the helm values to set the key provider type.
[05:06] Priya Menon: any differences in latency when using HSM?
[05:09] Ethan Ruiz: minimal — key unwrap operations are done on session setup; per-token cryptography isn't routed to HSM. so you'll see a small hit during boot or rekey, not per request.
[05:18] Zoe Park: for the marketplace listing, does Redwood certify the operator for automatic upgrades? if we push a cluster policy will it auto-upgrade?
[05:25] Nora Patel: we support both manual and automatic upgrade channels. marketplace listing bundles a stable chart and we put an upgrade policy in annotations. automatic upgrades are opt-in and we require a canary first.
[05:35] Carlos Diaz: about canaries — can we run a canary in a separate namespace and keep traffic isolated?
[05:39] Ethan Ruiz: yes we recommend canary namespacing and our operator supports weighted traffic routing. note: for private deployments you own the routing; for hosted we can orchestrate weighted rollouts.
[05:50] Priya Menon: Onboarding timeline question: if we start UAT next week, what's the typical time to production? 4 weeks?
[05:56] Maya Chen: typical path for customers of your size is 3—6 weeks depending on compliance and perf gates. given you want HSM and some KMS constraints, i'd budget 5 weeks.
[06:04] Priya Menon: ok.
[06:06] Speaker 6: (crosstalk)
[06:10] Maya Chen: ok let's dig into the helm values. Ethan, you wanna walk folks through sample values?
[06:14] Ethan Ruiz: sure. i'll screen share now (note: transcription may miss some screen details). key knobs: image.tag, enableKMS, kms.provider, secrets.backend (k8s|sealed|csi), enableCacheWarmup, cache.size, storageClass. For marketplace you'll fill out marketplace.* keys for listing metadata and subscription mapping.
[06:36] Priya Menon: there's a field called marketplace.callbackUrl — is that required?
[06:39] Ethan Ruiz: only for hosted marketplace installs where the console needs to receive lifecycle callbacks. if you're running private in your VPC it's not required.
[06:46] Carlos Diaz: what about RBAC? i'm worried about over-privileged service accounts.
[06:50] Ethan Ruiz: we tried to follow least privilege; the operator needs cluster-level CRD permissions and certain rolebindings for node-level tasks. we provide a minimal RBAC file and an expanded one. you can tweak the rolebinding scope.
[07:04] Liam O'Neill: How do we ensure audit logs are shipped to our SIEM? do you push logs or do we pull?
[07:11] Nora Patel: we support both. the operator can forward logs to your syslog endpoint or push to S3 for ingestion. we also support Fluent Bit sidecar to ship to your ELK/Datadog.
[07:22] Priya Menon: Will you share the log schema and a sample dev env artifact?
[07:25] Maya Chen: yes, action item there.
[07:28] Carlos Diaz: small nit: our cluster uses restricted podSecurityPolicy, any known conflicts?
[07:33] Ethan Ruiz: the operator requires privileged syscalls for fastpack kernel modules in some older runtimes; if you run fully restricted we have a non-privileged path but with lower perf. we'll note that in compatibility matrix.
[07:45] Zoe Park: question — do you do model pinning at install time? we need predictable provenance.
[07:49] Ethan Ruiz: yes you can pin modelVersion in values. for marketplace we also provide a mapping UI to pin to certified model bundles.
[07:56] Priya Menon: Ok — let's capture the UAT plan here: - DeltaForge will spin up two-node k8s cluster, enable CSI and have Vault set up. - Redwood will supply helm chart and runbook, plus pre-warm job. - Performance run target: 100 rps embeddings p95 < 250ms, 10 rps gen p95 < 600ms. Anything missing?
[08:20] Maya Chen: add network diagram and firewall rules and we'll add preflight checklist success criteria.
[08:26] Priya Menon: yes.
[08:28] Carlos Diaz: small question on license keys, do marketplace installs need license activation?
[08:32] Maya Chen: marketplace ledger will handle license entitlements via the marketplace token, but for private/air-gapped we have an offline license file.
[08:40] Liam O'Neill: are there any telemetry endpoints that leak org identifiers? we need to make sure PII isn't sent.
[08:46] Nora Patel: we redact PII by default, we can toggle full telemetry if you opt-in for debugging.
[08:53] Zoe Park: can the connector run in amber mode if connectivity to Redwood is lost, so we degrade gracefully?
[08:59] Ethan Ruiz: yes, we've got an offline-fallback policy: local evals continue with cached models and telemetry is buffered. for hosted control-plane installs we recommend a fallback model variant for critical paths.
[09:12] Priya Menon: great. last few mins — any blocker items from your side?
[09:16] Carlos Diaz: i need the RBAC minimal yaml and the preflight script.
[09:19] Liam O'Neill: i need the audit schema and KMS/HSM integration notes.
[09:22] Priya Menon: i'll send the network diagram and provide dates for the test cluster.
[09:26] Maya Chen: perfect. Recap: we'll share helm chart + runbook + RBAC + audit schema by Thurs 4/14. Ethan will own scheduling the UAT perf window, target week of 4/19. Priya will provide network diagram by 4/16. Liam will review KMS constraints and liaise on HSM choices.
[09:46] Zoe Park: thanks all. 
[09:49] Speaker 6: bye
[09:51] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.
